findings.reason: merge.js:27-32 now sends any empty, unowned collection with one source to collection.constructor(iters[0]). For a plain Record that is RecordType (Record.js:102), which builds a new instance (Record.js:56-57, 91-95), so the locked test __tests__/issues.ts:131-136 (expect(emptyRecord.merge({id:1})).toBe(emptyRecord)) fails. For a class that extends Record({}), constructor is the ES class, and calling it without new throws a TypeError; the tests do use Record subclasses (Record.ts:172, RecordJS.js:35). Both reviewers describe the same removed guard, so the findings are merged.
findings.claim: Removing the isRecord guard means merging a nonempty source into an empty Record no longer returns the same record: a plain empty Record gets a new instance (failing the locked Issue #1785 test), and an empty Record subclass throws.
findings.evidence: The diff deletes `import { isRecord }` and replaces `return isRecord(collection) ? collection // Record is empty and will not be updated: return the same instance : collection.constructor(iters[0]);` with `return collection.constructor(iters[0]);`. For a Record, `constructor` is RecordType (src/Record.js:102). With no keys, RecordType calls `l.set(this._indices[k], ...)` with `_indices[k]` undefined (src/Record.js:91-95), so the empty record gets a new instance or a malformed `_values` list. The locked test __tests__/issues.ts:131-136 ('Issue #1785 merge() should not return undefined') asserts `expect(emptyRecord.merge({ id: 1 })).toBe(emptyRecord)`, and that identity check cannot pass with this code. acceptance.md says the baseline's tests are the locked acceptance tests.
